name: Reactionary modernism
summary: Reactionary modernism, a term coined by Jeffrey Herf, names the Weimar-era German right's fusion of enthusiasm for modern technology, industry and war with rejection of the Enlightenment, liberalism and parliamentary democracy. Its thinkers wanted a strong, hierarchical, Volkisch national state that would harness machines and mass mobilisation in the service of myth, duty and national rebirth, and many were absorbed into or supported Nazism.
scope: Herf's German strand: the Conservative Revolution and engineer-ideologues of the Weimar Republic and Third Reich, centred on Ernst Juenger, Oswald Spengler, Carl Schmitt, Hans Freyer and Werner Sombart. Excludes later applications to Islamism or the digerati; Juenger and Spengler were not Nazis, so racial and some welfare answers reflect the wider Nazi-aligned mainstream and are often inferred.

keyFigures.name: Ernst Jünger
keyFigures.role: Writer whose total mobilisation and worker essays celebrated war and technology.

keyFigures.name: Oswald Spengler
keyFigures.role: Philosopher of history who urged Prussian socialism and a technics-embracing Faustian West.

keyFigures.name: Carl Schmitt
keyFigures.role: Jurist who justified dictatorship, the exception and the Nazi leader state.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Herf's thinkers embraced eugenic medicine and a state-run national body, but none addressed health insurance; adherents could go either way, so this is an unresolved inference.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Spengler's Prussian socialism ordered pay by rank and achievement and opposed progressive taxation and state insurance, so a statutory wage floor is not part of it; inferred.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Spengler held that the state should oversee the national productive structure, and the Conservative Revolution sought to control the greed of capital, so the movement rejected laissez-faire.

public-ownership.rationale: Spengler said true socialism would leave property and enterprise in private hands under state oversight, so outright public ownership of industry was not the program.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Spengler opposed progressive taxation, though he wanted capital subordinated to the state; an inference for a typical adherent.

unions-good.rationale: The movement wanted occupational bodies integrated into the state and rejected class-struggle organisation; independent unions as class instruments do not fit, though the Nazi state incorporated labour.

property-fundamental.rationale: Property was kept but subordinated to the national productive order, so it is not a near-inviolable right.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Edgar Jung and others wanted the greed of capital controlled by the state while keeping private ownership, which implies tighter regulation.

cut-welfare.rationale: Spengler opposed state insurance, yet the Nazi regime ran a large national welfare apparatus for the Volk; adherents split.

worker-ownership.rationale: Spengler's socialism was explicitly not seizure of firms, and the Conservative Revolution rejected Marxist and syndicalist ownership schemes.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Schmitt's primacy of security and the exception, and the authoritarian state generally, imply acceptance of surveillance; the thinkers did not discuss it directly.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Jünger himself experimented with drugs later, but the Weimar-right milieu stressed discipline and hardness; the typical adherent would oppose legalisation (inferred).

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: The ideology was itself a hostile-to-liberalism movement and the Third Reich used racist myth openly; speech limits defined by liberal norms would not be endorsed, though the regime censored heavily.

strong-leader.rationale: Schmitt held that every capable government needs a dictatorial element and, in 1934, that the Fuhrer protects the law; Spengler anticipated a long era of dictatorial rule.

state-harmful.rationale: Schmitt, Spengler and Jünger all demanded a strong, militarily prepared, hierarchical state; none was anti-statist.

limit-guns.rationale: Not discussed; the Nazi state armed loyal citizens and disarmed enemies, and Jünger's soldier-worker ethos favours martial culture, so no clear position.

empower-police-military.rationale: Jünger wanted a state that is socially oriented, militarily prepared and hierarchically structured, and the movement sought to carry military values into peacetime.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: The Conservative Revolution stressed discipline and moral instinct against urban decadence; legalisation is inferred as unwelcome.

decide-locally.rationale: Schmitt and the movement favoured a unified, sovereign national authority over federal or local dispersal.

rehabilitation.rationale: Schmitt's emphasis on order and hardness suggests punishment over rehabilitation; the sources do not take it up, so this is inferred.

traditional-family.rationale: Spengler placed morality in instinct and rural life against the artificial city, and the Third Reich promoted a pronatalist family ideal.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Spengler's inherited, instinctive morality and the Nazi regime's persecution of homosexuals make legal same-sex marriage unthinkable for an adherent.

abortion-legal.rationale: The movement and the Third Reich were pronatalist and treated reproduction as a national duty, so legal abortion is rejected.

more-religion-public.rationale: Thinkers rejected Christian egalitarian ethics and some Volkisch currents wanted a Germanic religion, while Schmitt prized political theology; adherents split.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Griffin and Herf describe racist myth as a core resource of the movement, so active redress of racial injustice is rejected.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Spengler held morality and character to be inherited through breeding rather than reflection, so the claim that gender is primarily constructed is rejected.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Moeller van den Bruck tied eternal values to the Volk and the movement's new nationalism was centred on national culture.

gradual-change.rationale: Moeller van den Bruck explicitly rejected the reactionary who only restores and wanted institutional forms radically redesigned; the movement spoke of revolution, not gradualism.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Volkisch nationalism defined the nation ethnically, so reducing immigration follows; the sources do not discuss immigration levels in modern terms.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Herf stresses the Sonderweg idea of Germany standing apart from the liberal West, and Schmitt attacked liberal internationalism.

free-trade.rationale: Spengler wanted the state directing the national economy, and the movement's autarkic nationalism opposed liberal free trade.

nation-first.rationale: Herf describes a Volkisch nationalism with Germany as a distinct central power outside East and West.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Schmitt attacked humanitarian universalism as a cover for power politics, so an adherent would reject rights-based war.

open-borders.rationale: The nationalist, Volkisch core of the ideology is incompatible with open borders.

limit-growth.rationale: Reactionary modernism prized industrial and technological growth as national power; limiting it for the environment contradicts the core.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Not a period concern; the technological-nationalist orientation would resist sweeping state climate controls, inferred.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Herf's thesis is enthusiasm for modern technology, though Spengler was gloomy about its fate, so agreement is moderate rather than strong.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Not an issue in the period; the technological enthusiasm and national power logic imply support.

revolution-justified.rationale: The movement was called the Conservative Revolution and explicitly sought a radical overturn of the Weimar order.

experts-over-public.rationale: Herf shows engineers presented as ideologues and the movement wanted an elite wielding intellectual power rather than mass opinion.

central-planning.rationale: Spengler wanted state oversight of the productive structure but kept property and enterprise; adherents were split on full planning.

socialized-markets.rationale: The movement's socialism kept private property under state direction rather than worker or public ownership; inferred.

land-value-tax.rationale: Spengler opposed progressive tax schemes and nothing links the movement to Georgism; inferred.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Spengler insisted that inheritance and property remain intact under Prussian socialism.

basic-income.rationale: Spengler's socialism ranked people by achievement and duty, which sits badly with an unconditional income; inferred.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Nationalist economic autarky and state direction of industry imply protection, though sources speak only generally.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Spengler had the state overseeing the national productive structure, and the Third Reich directed industry toward strategic ends.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The movement was modernist and industrial rather than agrarian-distributist; some Volkisch strands favoured peasants, so this is a weak inference.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Spengler explicitly kept property, inheritance and personal enterprise and called Marxism the capitalism of the working class.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Nothing in the sources; the state-directed economy suggests control of money, not its removal.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Spengler proposed occupational bodies and revocable mandates in place of parties, and the Third Reich imposed a Labour Front corporatist order.

one-party-rule.rationale: Spengler wanted no parties and a dictator, and the Third Reich became one-party; adherents differed on whether rule needed a party at all.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The movement was split between those nostalgic for monarchy and those wanting a new leader state; Moeller van den Bruck opposed mere restoration.

democracy-best.rationale: Jünger said he hated democracy like the plague and the movement widely rejected parliamentary democracy.

direct-votes.rationale: Schmitt favoured plebiscitary acclamation of a leader, not citizens legislating by vote; mass voting on laws is not endorsed.

workers-councils.rationale: Spengler rejected Marxist and council socialism, and the movement wanted political power in a state, not in workers' bodies.

right-to-secede.rationale: A sovereign, unified national state is central to Schmitt and the movement, so regional secession is rejected.

natural-rulers.rationale: The movement sought elite rule and Spengler said achievement and talent set rank; Jünger wanted a young intellectual elite to lead.

political-violence-never.rationale: Jünger glorified war and the front soldier, and the movement endorsed violence as a political instrument.

war-builds-character.rationale: Jünger portrayed war as a mystical revealing experience and wanted military values carried into peacetime.

separate-church-state.rationale: Schmitt thought modern state concepts were secularised theology, but he and others were not committed to a church-led state; split.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: The movement was mostly secular or neo-pagan in its Volkisch strands and rejected Christian egalitarian ethics.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Schmitt's theory is built on the state's monopoly of decision and force, so privatised courts and defence are rejected.

military-superiority.rationale: Jünger wanted a militarily prepared state and German great-power status, and Spengler thought the West's survival required strength.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Herf describes Volkisch nationalism central to the movement, though Jünger and Spengler were not simple biological racists.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Spengler contrasted his duty-based socialism to English class-conflict socialism, and Marxism's materialism was dismissed as outdated.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Spengler said socialism means rank by achievement and talent, not levelling by wealth.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Not discussed; the nationalist and hierarchical outlook would not grant such authority, inferred.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Not addressed in period; the great-power nationalism of the movement would reject reparations for colonialism.

civilizational-union.rationale: The Sonderweg thinking made Germany a distinct centre; some saw a Central European bloc, others a purely national path.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Prussian socialism prized duty, service and subordination of the individual to the state over self-interest.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Spengler's Prussian socialism rested on duty, command and obedience as against liberal individual rights.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: The technological romantic outlook viewed nature as material for national power, though romantic and Volkisch strands loved the land; weakly inferred.

limit-population.rationale: The movement and regime were pronatalist and viewed national strength as depending on numbers.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Herf's whole thesis is that these thinkers embraced industrial technology, whatever their other complaints about modernity.

accelerate-technology.rationale: They embraced technology but tied it to a national and authoritarian order, so disruption of institutions was acceptable only against liberal ones.

human-enhancement.rationale: Eugenic medicine was embraced, yet individual freedom to modify oneself conflicts with state direction; split.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Anachronistic; technocratic enthusiasm and distrust of the mass public point one way, hierarchy of human leaders another.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: A state with sovereign authority over security would reject citizen-held secrets beyond its reach; inferred.

restore-past-order.rationale: Moeller van den Bruck rejected the reactionary who only restores, and Herf's concept is about reconciling modernity with reaction.

results-over-ideology.rationale: The movement was passionately ideological and mythic; pragmatic ideology-free policy is not its style.

direct-action.rationale: The movement distrusted parliaments and Jünger's wartime milieu glorified decisive action, though the Nazi route used elections too.

means-match-ends.rationale: Schmitt's decisionism justified any means for order; the statement is inferred as rejected.

return-to-foraging.rationale: The ideology embraced advanced technology and industry as national power.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Spengler's Prussian socialism rests on hierarchy of rank and function, which presupposes division of labour.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Spengler's rank by achievement and talent contradicts distribution by need.

production-for-use.rationale: Production for national strength is the goal, though profit was not abolished; adherents partly agree.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Spengler called Marxism the capitalism of the working class and rejected its exploitation theory.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Spengler rejected Marxist socialism and class rule in favour of a national, hierarchical state.

collective-farming.rationale: The Volkisch milieu valued the peasant on his own land, and the sources show no collectivism.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: The movement rejected Marxist analysis and Spengler thought war arises from the nature of life and nations.

taxation-theft.rationale: Taxation serving a sovereign state is basic to Schmitt's and Spengler's statism.

harm-principle.rationale: Schmitt rejected liberal limits on the state and the movement rejected liberalism wholesale.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Prussian socialism and Volkisch thought put the community and nation before individual rights.

conscription.rationale: Jünger sought military structures and values carried into peacetime and total mobilisation of the population.

exit-over-voice.rationale: The movement stressed membership in the national community, not exit as a check on rulers.

state-as-business.rationale: Spengler's state ordered by duty and command is the opposite of a customer-service state.

positive-liberty.rationale: Spengler's socialism has the state organise opportunity by rank, but freedom claims in liberal terms were rejected; split.

media-academia-power.rationale: Dupeux describes the movement's aim as gaining intellectual power to spread its ideas, which implies attention to cultural institutions; inferred.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Spengler held morality inherited through breeding and Volkisch racialism was part of the milieu, though the cited authors differ on biological racism.

organic-representation.rationale: Spengler called for occupational bodies and rejected parties and periodic elections.

total-state.rationale: Jünger's total mobilisation and the totalitarian state described by Griffin direct every sphere of life including the economy.

national-rebirth.rationale: Moeller van den Bruck and the Conservative Revolution framed Germany as needing a radical renewal, and Griffin describes fascism's palingenetic project.

territorial-expansion.rationale: The Sonderweg and the Third Reich pursued expansion, though Jünger framed nationalism as an explosive, not an absolute.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: The Fuhrer principle resembles personal loyalty but not feudal oaths; split.

bound-labor.rationale: Feudal bondage is premodern; the movement was modernist, but the regime used forced labour; inferred as rejected in principle.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Spengler said we no longer believe in the power of reason over life, and Griffin notes the use of consciously manipulated myth.

universal-morality.rationale: The movement rejected the Enlightenment and universal egalitarian morality, preferring morality as inherited, instinctive and national.

single-common-good.rationale: Schmitt held that the political unity of the people is defined by a sovereign decision against pluralist bargaining.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Nazi and Volkisch antisemitism and the regime's antisemitic politics make endorsement of a Jewish state unlikely, though not a stated doctrine.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Not addressed; the Nazi regime promoted ethnic Germans abroad, but a general right is not stated.

revive-national-language.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; the nationalist outlook is sympathetic but German had no need of revival.

workplace-democracy.rationale: The movement ordered workplaces by rank and leadership, as Spengler's command and obedience.

school-vouchers.rationale: The totalising state directs education, so parent choice is unlikely; inferred.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: The sources do not address fiscal policy; the regime ran heavy deficit spending but Spengler opposed some state intervention.

economic-freedom.rationale: The movement held that the state oversees the economy and political order comes first.

rule-by-example.rationale: Jünger emphasised heroic, sacrificing elites as models, but authoritarian movements also relied on laws and force; weak agreement.

national-self-determination.rationale: The Volkisch nationalism of the movement affirms national self-rule, but its Sonderweg also justified German expansion.

force-without-un.rationale: Schmitt rejected the claim of international bodies to limit sovereign decisions on war and the exception.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Spengler said we no longer believe in the power of reason over life, and the movement rejected the Enlightenment.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: A Volkisch national community would limit benefits to its members.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Spengler's socialism rests on duty and achievement, which favours work obligations.

class-collaboration.rationale: Spengler's Prussian socialism and the corporatist order set employers and workers in one national body of duty, not class conflict.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: The movement sought to preserve eternal national values, though Futurist strands glorified machinery; adherents split but mainly oppose.

dominated-front.rationale: The Sonderweg placed Germany between East and West and resentful of the West, but no common front of dominated states was proposed.

workers-nation.rationale: Jünger's front-soldier socialism and Spengler's national socialism joined workers to the nation instead of an international class.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Spengler's instinct-based morality and the regime's gender order assigned distinct roles.

ban-interest.rationale: Spengler explicitly kept capital accumulation; the Nazi slogan of breaking interest-slavery was a minor strand.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The Third Reich classified by race and separated groups in law, which Griffin describes as built on racist myth.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Spengler and Schmitt treat the state as an autonomous sovereign above classes, the opposite of the Marxist view.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: National industrial strength and autarky favour domestic energy, inferred.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: The Volkisch ethnic nation sees assimilation as impossible for outsiders, yet the movement wanted cultural conformity; split.

elite-replacement.rationale: The conspiracy of this kind is a later idea; Nazi antisemitic conspiracism was strong but not this immigration claim.

proportional-representation.rationale: Spengler wanted no parties or periodic elections and the movement rejected Weimar's party parliament.

national-mission.rationale: The Sonderweg idea gave Germany a distinct mission, though it was not about spreading a form of government.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Schmitt attacked party politics as hammered out in smoke-filled rooms, which is the movement's staple critique of Weimar politicians.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Herf names eugenics-based medicine as one of the modern practices the movement embraced.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Schmitt justified the Night of the Long Knives killings as protection of law, so accountability for state killings was rejected.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Jünger wanted a state organising life by mobilisation, not a minimal one.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: The racist myth Griffin describes included racial separation, and the regime criminalised mixed marriage.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The movement rejected Christian egalitarian ethics and Enlightenment equality in favour of hierarchy.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Spengler's national socialism is built for one country, not for revolution abroad, so the claim is opposed.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Not addressed; the movement's expansionist outlook would reject this framing.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Not discussed; a unified state would favour it but religion was not a central issue.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Not addressed; the movement's concern was race and Volk, not conversion.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: There is no link between the movement and cattle protection.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Divided between secular, Christian and neo-pagan strands; no stated position.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Marxist-Leninist theory; the movement believed in a strengthened state against enemies, but the premise is not its own.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Schmitt held that the sovereign decides and the Fuhrer's authority replaces a formal constitution, rather than rest on consent.

trade-surplus.rationale: Autarkic nationalist economics favours export strength, inferred.

population-transfer.rationale: The Third Reich forced out and deported groups it saw as hostile, and Volkisch nationalism implies it.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Jünger glorified war and the movement considered force an instrument of politics.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Jünger's total mobilisation sees struggle and war as the shaping force of the modern age, and Spengler framed peoples' histories as struggles.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Schmitt supported defending the constitutional order by exceptional measures and the regime outlawed rivals.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Republican freedom theory is liberal-adjacent; Schmitt's sovereign decision is dominating by design.

separated-powers.rationale: Schmitt held the liberal separation of powers to be at odds with democracy as identity of rulers and ruled.

vanguard-party.rationale: Marxist-Leninist idea; Spengler rejected parties, though the Nazi party acted as a vanguard.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Rank by achievement and talent, not priority to the poor, though the Volksgemeinschaft promised care for the nation's members.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Class collaboration and state-organised labour implied no independent strikes; the Third Reich banned them.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Pronatalism and Lebensraum thought held that numbers are strength; poverty was blamed on liberal and Jewish economics.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Volkisch nationalism holds that national unity depends on common blood and culture.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: The movement wanted rule by an elite and leader, not random selection.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Schmitt defined the sovereign as who decides the exception and praised Article 48 emergency powers.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: State direction of the productive structure permits price controls, inferred.

party-controls-media.rationale: The Third Reich centralised propaganda and media, and Jünger-type elites aimed at intellectual power.

party-commands-army.rationale: Jünger disliked Nazi mass politics, and the military tradition prized an independent officer corps; split.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Volkisch nationalism makes citizenship hard to gain, inferred.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Rank by achievement did not imply pay equalisation for officials.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Command and obedience as basic principle, though Spengler wanted no parties.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Schmitt and the Volkisch right rejected supranational limits on sovereign German power.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Schmitt's Reich president and Fuhrer model placed the armed forces and the government under one leader.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Schmitt admired the Church's hierarchy but the movement had no church doctrine.

clerical-rule.rationale: The movement sought rule by a political and military elite, not clergy.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Jünger's front community and the nationalist right held that all must serve the nation at war.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Weimar's 'return to order' condemned degenerate culture, and the regime later censored art, though modernist art was also embraced.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Schmitt supported a leader with lasting plebiscitary authority.

recall-officials.rationale: Spengler proposed revocable mandates within occupational bodies, a partial agreement, but recall by voters is not endorsed.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: The Sonderweg and neutrality in East/West blocs versus Nazi alliances; split.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Spengler's property remained intact and the movement did not seek such a levelling.

people-in-arms.rationale: Jünger's total mobilisation and the people under arms; yet the officer corps stayed professional; weak agreement.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Spengler placed instinct and morality in rural life against the artificial city.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Volkisch nationalism sought to unite all Germans in one Reich, as in Austria and the Sudetenland.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: The movement itself was intellectual, though it despised literati of the liberal sort.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Spengler held cultures to be organic and incommensurable, yet saw Faustian West as distinctive; mixed but the Volkisch hierarchy rejects equal.

death-penalty.rationale: Schmitt justified summary killings by the state and the regime used the death penalty widely.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: The Weimar-right milieu opposed liberal sex reform, inferred.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: The ideology embraced modern science and technology, so creationism is not part of it.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Moral discipline against urban decadence, inferred.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Volkisch nationalism defines the nation by descent.

minority-language-support.rationale: Nationalist unity favours one language, though the topic is not addressed.

religious-exemptions.rationale: A unified state demanding loyalty would not exempt minorities.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Jünger said each life becomes the life of a worker, and the movement rejected liberal individuality.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Germans resented reparations, but cancellation of debts as a general policy was not stated.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Not a concern; autarkic nationalism might agree.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Schmitt's constituent power rests in the people's will expressed by acclamation, not a representative assembly; inferred.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Herf's movement combined authoritarianism with rapid industrial development.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Spengler saw technology reaching coloured peoples as a danger and held nationhood first.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: The great-power nationalism would favour independence, anachronistic.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Spengler's inherited, instinct-based morality and the regime's gender order treated male-led roles as natural, not as systematic disadvantage to women.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Schmitt favoured a plebiscitary president acclaimed by the people over parliamentary selection, as in his defence of the Reich president.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Spengler wanted the state to oversee the national economy, which implies subordinating money to political authority; inferred.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Volkisch nationalism treats national territory as non-negotiable, though the sources do not discuss peace deals.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Spengler kept property but under state oversight of the national productive order, and the movement sought to control capital's greed.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Spengler called Marxism the capitalism of the working class, which leans to this view, but the thinkers wrote little on the USSR as such.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Technological enthusiasm and state-power priorities make caution-first environmental rules unlikely; inferred.

collective-defense.rationale: The Sonderweg and the Third Reich made alliances opportunistically; no stated doctrine.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: The Third Reich annexed territory by force; adherents would deny unlawfulness where it served the nation.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Schmitt's sovereign state takes precedence over churches in the final decision, though he admired the Church; weakly agreed.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Schmitt's Reich president was meant as a guardian above party politics, an idea the movement shared against Weimar parties.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Sovereign unity of the state is core to Schmitt and the movement, so force is accepted to preserve it.

region-keeps-system.rationale: The centralising totalising state leaves no room for regional distinct systems; inferred.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Schmitt's political theology treats sovereignty as quasi-sacred and the Fuhrer cult approached it, but divine descent was no doctrine.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Spengler opposed progressive taxation but the movement as a whole had no tax-rate policy.

character-from-environment.rationale: Spengler held morality to be instinctive and inherited through breeding, not formed by circumstances.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Schmitt's sovereign is the one who decides the exception beyond the legal order, and the Fuhrer's will replaced formal constitution.

space-expansion.rationale: Anachronistic; technological romanticism might welcome it as national feat, but no source speaks to it.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Schmitt and the movement wanted concentrated sovereign authority, though elites and leader were combined.

leader-cult.rationale: Schmitt's justification of the Fuhrer's authority and the Third Reich's mass leader worship embody this position.

equal-parenting.rationale: No source addresses it and distinct gender roles cut against it; split.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Spengler rejected class struggle altogether; nor did party leaders restoring capitalism fit his view.

land-redistribution.rationale: Property and inheritance remain intact under Prussian socialism.

refugee-return.rationale: The Third Reich expelled populations, and adherents would resist the right of return of hostile groups; inferred.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Volkisch nationalism sought to unite Germans outside the Reich, and the Third Reich used this claim for Austria and the Sudetenland.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: The movement had no religious law; neo-pagan and secular strands would not punish it.

women-must-cover.rationale: Not a concern of the movement; inferred.

common-currency.rationale: The Sonderweg and economic nationalism favour a national currency.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: The Volkisch idea of pan-German unification fits this, and the Reich sought to unite Germans.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: A unified national state demanding loyalty leaves no space for autonomous minority institutions.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Nazi policy pressured minorities to leave, so equal-rights-in-place is contrary to its view.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Spengler dismissed Marx's materialist science as outdated and said we no longer believe in the power of reason over life.

ban-cartels.rationale: State-directed industry in the Third Reich forced cartels; breaking up concentration for competition is not the aim.

no-bailouts.rationale: The state directing the productive structure would support firms important to the nation; inferred.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Schmitt attacked liberal constitutional limits and held that the people's unified will, as acclaimed, rules.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: The regime and thinkers held distinct gender roles in public life.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: The Sonderweg's German-centred bloc and Nazi autarky aimed at self-sufficiency.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Supranational standards would intrude on sovereignty.

moral-incentives.rationale: Spengler's Prussian socialism stresses duty and service as the spur to work.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Conservative Revolution thinkers and the Freikorps milieu saw small determined minorities as the agent of change.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The movement favoured hierarchy by rank and talent; Spengler kept inheritance, so hereditary privilege was not attacked.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Moeller van den Bruck tied eternal values to the Volk, and Spengler's morphology centred on the Faustian West.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Not directly addressed; the hierarchical racialist worldview supports it.

patriotic-education.rationale: Moeller van den Bruck's new nationalism and the regime's schooling aimed at loyalty to the nation.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Racial hierarchy in its own favour, not meritocracy, but the opposition to preferences for minorities is inferred.

public-money-creation.rationale: State oversight of money fits some strands, private banking critique was a Nazi theme, but the sources do not state it.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Spengler thought capitalism needed state oversight, not that it would collapse of itself; split.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Great-power nationalism implies it; the Weimar right wanted colonies and the Reich's earlier reach back.

delink-world-market.rationale: Autarky for Germany was favoured, but for poor countries nothing is said.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A Marxist category the movement did not use.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: The movement endorsed state-enforced discrimination rather than private freedom.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Schmitt attacked liberal constitutionalism and treated rights as subject to the sovereign decision.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Germany lost its colonies at Versailles and resented that treaty, but adherents had no stated view on others' treaties.

elective-rulers.rationale: Schmitt held authority to come from sovereign decision and acclamation, not ordinary elections; though hereditary rule was not required either.

minority-veto.rationale: Schmitt's decisionism and the leader principle reject any minority veto.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Schmitt put the sovereign above the legal order, so subjects have no right of resistance.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Schmitt criticised parliamentary democracy and the movement rejected it.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Not addressed; the Third Reich passed animal-protection laws, but the thinkers did not take it up.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Inferred from the modern technological outlook and the regime's animal-protection laws permitting use.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Spengler's duty-based Prussian socialism has the privileged owing service to the state and nation, though not welfare to the poor as such.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Jünger's total mobilisation draws every life into the work of the nation; withdrawal is the opposite of it.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: The movement attacked liberal mass culture yet used mass politics itself.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: A Gramscian theory the movement did not use, but its manipulation of myth (Griffin) fits partly.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: The Sonderweg complaint was that Germany was exploited by Versailles, but dependency theory is not part of it.

native-born-offices.rationale: Volkisch nationalism reserves public life to members of the nation.

return-lost-territory.rationale: The Weimar right made revision of the Versailles borders a central demand, and the Third Reich acted on it.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Not discussed; the national-ethnic hierarchy would not support it elsewhere.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Reactionary modernism is the Weimar right and fascism's own intellectual formation, so anti-fascism as founding value is against it.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: The movement embraced totalitarian state as positive and saw communism as enemy, not an equal.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: National tradition and its heroes are preserved by Moeller van den Bruck's nationalism; inferred.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Not discussed; distinct gender roles but not a stated view.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Herf stresses the Sonderweg idea that Germany needed its own path rather than Western liberal institutions.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Jünger wanted military values and structures at the centre of the state, and the Reichswehr's political role was welcomed by the right.

paid-care-work.rationale: Distinct gender roles in family are favoured over paid care labour; inferred.

filial-duty.rationale: Spengler's duty ethic and the traditional-family emphasis imply it.

office-by-exam.rationale: Prussian bureaucratic tradition favoured trained officials, but leader loyalty counted for more.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: National economic control over strategic industry follows from the movement's economic nationalism.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Traditional family emphasis, though the Nazi state liberalised some divorce on racial grounds; inferred.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Spengler proposed revocable mandates in occupational bodies, but leader command rejects binding delegates generally.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: State insurance was opposed by Spengler, so private accounts might fit, but the Third Reich's collective approach prevails.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Property and inheritance stay intact under Spengler's socialism.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Schmitt backed presidential emergency powers over parliament, and parliamentary control of the budget was rejected.

single-official-language.rationale: The Volkisch nation is built on one national culture and language.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: National control of land follows from Volkisch nationalism and economic autarky.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Racial hierarchy is accepted, so unequal outcomes are not discrimination.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: The movement condemned bourgeois materialism, and Spengler stressed duty over wealth.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Not stated; the Third Reich used proxies.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Great-power domination of its sphere is consistent with Schmitt's Grossraum idea; weakly agreed.

corporate-influence.rationale: The movement wanted the state above capital but also embraced industry as national asset.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: National sovereignty above foreign influence follows from Volkisch nationalism.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Spengler and the movement saw a large national population as strength, and the Reich offered marriage and child incentives.

residents-only-property.rationale: The sources never discuss local property purchase limits, and a centralising national state cuts against local discretion while Volkisch logic favours native control; split.

job-guarantee.rationale: Spengler's duty ethic and Nazi work programmes imply state provision of work.

democratic-peace.rationale: Schmitt rejected liberal universalism and saw democracy-promotion as ideology; the movement rejected democracy.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Spengler's Prussian socialism rests on command, obedience and duty to the state.

non-intervention.rationale: Schmitt supported great-power spheres; the sovereign decision on war is unrestrained.

industrial-unions.rationale: Occupational bodies were preferred to unions, craft or industry.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Nazi antisemitism treated Jews as a conspiratorial enemy, and Herf notes the movement tied technology to Germans rather than Jews.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Traditional family structures are central to the movement.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Secrecy and arcana of state are a part of Schmitt's sovereign decision.

informal-organisation.rationale: The movement favoured disciplined hierarchical organisation.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Schmitt asserted sovereign national decision over international law, and the Sonderweg stance rejects Western norms.

religious-nation.rationale: The nation was defined by blood and Volk, not religion.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: The Sonderweg idea claims German independence; but Grossraum would demand deference from others to Germany, so mixed.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: A unified centralising state controls revenue.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Spengler kept all property including means of production.

defeat-communism.rationale: The Conservative Revolution and the Third Reich opposed Marxist and internationalist socialism as an enemy.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Spengler wanted state oversight with private enterprise intact, which loosely fits a mix, but service delivery was never discussed.

religion-illusion.rationale: Schmitt saw religious concepts as the root of state theory; the movement valued myth, not unmasking religion.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Spengler praised capital accumulation and competition but under state oversight.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Distinct roles for women are favoured; economic transformation for equality is no goal.

socialized-care.rationale: Family care was a female role in the regime's view, though the state had mass services.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Volkisch language purism was part of the cultural nationalism of the milieu, though the cited sources do not state it.

treaties-binding.rationale: Schmitt put sovereign decision above treaty obligations.

cooperative-communities.rationale: The movement embraced large-scale industrial state.

majority-settlement.rationale: The Third Reich resettled Germans in the East, which follows Volkisch logic.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Spengler's Prussian socialism and Moeller van den Bruck's Third Reich idea offered a third course against Marxism and English capitalism.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Volkisch nationalism founds claim on the Volk's historic homeland, though not exclusively.

holocaust-denial.rationale: The sources do not discuss this; Jünger found Nazi treatment of Jews incompatible with honour, but the regime committed it.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: The Third Reich criminalised it and the traditional-moral milieu supported it.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Schmitt justified the Night of the Long Knives and the regime's suppression.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: The movement was not clerical; Volkisch strands had alternative religions.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Great-power nationalism implies it; Weimar right demanded colonies.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: An Islamic doctrine unrelated to the ideology; Herf notes later application to Islamism by others.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Jünger hated democracy and the movement rejected mass participation.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Racist myth and hierarchy are core, so this critical framework is rejected.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Instinctive inherited gender order is opposed to this.

assisted-dying.rationale: Eugenic medicine embraced, but euthanasia was a regime practice rather than a stated ideology position about patient choice; split.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Moeller van den Bruck and Spengler claimed to transcend left and right with a nationalist socialism.

alienated-labor.rationale: Marxist critique, but Jünger described the worker figure as modern man's fulfilment.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Schmitt saw state concepts as secularised theology and sovereignty as quasi-divine, but Nazi authority came from the Volk and Fuhrer.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: The sources are silent on religious dress; secular and Christian strands of the movement would diverge.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Workplace harassment rules lay outside the movement; no position can be drawn from its texts.

social-market-economy.rationale: State oversight of the economy with private property is similar, but liberal competition rules are not the aim.

rich-first.rationale: Spengler accepted competition and unequal accumulation under state oversight, but the sources do not address staged development.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: The Sonderweg meant Germany neither West nor East, which supports neutrality as a principle though the Reich later allied.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Leader principle favours chosen successor but the movement had no dynastic doctrine.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Spengler kept capital accumulation and competition.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Weimar right resented foreign financial claims on Germany (reparations); inferred.

property-franchise.rationale: The movement wanted rank by achievement and talent, not property qualification.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Spengler's morality and the technological outlook reject this ecofeminist claim.

reification.rationale: Marxist concept; Spengler rejected it, though Herf's critical-theory frame discusses it as critique of the movement, not its view.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Marxist-flavoured complaint; the movement attacked liberal press but did not blame wealth.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Schmitt attacked the rule-of-law state and the Fuhrer principle replaced fixed law with leader's decision.

racial-franchise.rationale: The Third Reich limited citizenship to Germans of the Volk and removed Jews' political rights.

open-government-data.rationale: Transparency is not part of a sovereign state of exception.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: The restriction in the regime was racial, not religious.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: The Nazi movement organised boycott of Jewish shops in 1933 and its antisemitic myth supported it.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Random citizens deliberating contradicts the elite and leader orientation.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Not an issue for the movement.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Spengler attacked plutocratic money-power, but the movement rejected liberal liberty as a goal, so adherents would not frame wealth as a threat to it; inferred and split.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: The movement prized a masculine soldierly ideal and the regime persecuted homosexuals, matching this audit's rejection of same-sex marriage.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Spengler and the Volkisch right valued myth, faith and tradition as sources of national will, so state atheism is unwelcome; inferred, though few wanted a religious state either.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: The movement wanted a strong, militarised, hierarchical state, and Schmitt justified coercive state power.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: The movement sought a unified Volkisch nation under authority and rejected party parliamentary bargaining, so guaranteed shares for communities are inferred to be unwelcome.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Spengler opposed state insurance, but the Nazi-aligned mainstream built party-run welfare; the sources do not address charity, so this is split and inferred.

term-limits.rationale: Hierarchical, leader-centred authority and rejection of periodic elections make limits on office-holding foreign to the movement; inferred from Spengler's and Juenger's politics.

vote-delegation.rationale: Spengler wanted no parties or periodic elections and the movement rejected parliamentary democracy, so a delegable citizen vote is a form of democracy it opposed.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: The movement glorified war, struggle and national rebirth over safety, so making extinction avoidance a top policy goal is inferred to conflict with its values.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: The movement's traditional, hierarchical and gendered order makes female clergy an unlikely demand; inferred, as religious office was not discussed.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Spengler's inherited, instinctive morality and the Nazi-aligned family ideal favoured male headship; inferred as marriage authority was not discussed.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Inferred from the Conservative Revolution's volkisch nationalism, which tied political membership to the nation.

rent-control.rationale: Spengler's Prussian socialism ordered economic life by rank and state authority; a rent cap is inferred to be tolerable to some but not a defining position.

abolish-ip.rationale: Not addressed; the technology-embracing school valued invention, but the sources do not discuss patents.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Inferred from Juenger's Total Mobilization and the Nazi-aligned mainstream of Herf's thinkers, who sought mass mobilisation for national service.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Not addressed; the school embraced modern military technology but the sources do not discuss basing.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Inferred from the Conservative Revolution's nationalism and revisionism against the Versailles order, which makes foreign garrisons objectionable.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Inferred; the Nazi-aligned mainstream rejected such recognition, but the sources do not discuss it.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Spengler's Prussian socialism ranks pay by duty and achievement and opposes unearned rentier income, but it is not a stated principle in the sources.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Inferred from Juenger's warrior ethos and the school's celebration of struggle and war.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Inferred from the volkisch myth of national rebirth; the Conservative Revolution invoked an ancient national essence.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Anachronistic; Herf's thinkers embraced biological and hierarchical conceptions, so a constructed sex would be rejected.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the school's traditional, hierarchical view of sex roles.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Juenger's front-line writings glorify sacrifice in war, and Herf's thinkers used myth and duty to sanctify death for the nation.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Schmitt's political theology and the school's appeal to myth frame politics as a struggle against enemies, though not strictly good against evil; inferred.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Inferred from the volkisch demand that the nation gather in one state, not stay dispersed.

culture-before-state.rationale: The Conservative Revolution called for spiritual and cultural rebirth as the base of the new state; inferred from its general outlook.

god-not-male.rationale: Anachronistic; the school's traditionalism is inferred to favour male descriptions.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the school's hierarchical, anti-liberal view of women's roles.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Inferred from the volkisch and Nazi-aligned insistence that the nation's economy serve the nation's own people.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Inferred from the volkisch aim of uniting a people in one state.

independent-unions.rationale: Inferred from the corporatist, hierarchical state that Herf's thinkers wanted, in which unions would be subordinate to it.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Spengler's Prussian socialism rejects class-based workers' power in favour of hierarchy, duty and service to the state.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Not addressed; adherents' state-centred approach could allow either public or private provision.

second-chamber.rationale: Inferred from Conservative Revolution thinkers' preference for corporatist and estate-based bodies over pure parliaments.

municipal-property.rationale: Inferred from the Volkisch nationalism and strong national state, which rejects local community ownership.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Inferred from the preference for a strong, centralised, hierarchical national state.

family-wage.rationale: Inferred from the Nazi-aligned mainstream's family and population policy; not stated by Juenger or Spengler.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Not addressed; no clear position follows.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Not addressed; no clear position follows, though Herf notes eugenic medicine.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Inferred from the authoritarian state's wish to control the economy and its citizens.

online-anonymity.rationale: Inferred from the authoritarian state's rejection of liberal privacy and its demand for mobilised, visible citizens.

person-over-state.rationale: Herf's thinkers rejected Enlightenment liberalism and individualism and subordinated the person to the national community.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Inferred from the reactionary rejection of materialism and appeals to myth, soul and national rebirth; Spengler's Man and Technics stresses spirit.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Inferred from the view that the national state is sovereign and any region's powers are its to grant.

gm-crops.rationale: Inferred from the embrace of modern technology and industry for national ends.

dense-cities.rationale: Not addressed; no clear position follows.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Inferred from the Volkisch outlook of the wider Nazi-aligned mainstream; Juenger and Spengler differ.

racial-pride.rationale: Inferred from the Volkisch outlook of the wider Nazi-aligned mainstream; Juenger and Spengler differ.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Juenger's Total Mobilization and the glorification of war in this strand see war as a source of national rebirth.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Not addressed directly; the volkisch nationalism of these thinkers fits a shared language and history making a people, though they stressed race and blood too.

communal-electorates.rationale: Inferred from their rejection of parliamentary pluralism in favour of a unified national state.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Inferred from the Weimar right's stab-in-the-back and Versailles encirclement narratives; not documented in the sources used.

free-public-college.rationale: Not addressed; these thinkers favoured elite, state-directed education, so inferred as unresolved.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from their embrace of industry and state direction over price-based restraint.

future-generations.rationale: Not addressed; national rebirth gives a duty to the nation's future but Juenger and Spengler were fatalist about decline, so split.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Inferred from their hard, martial ideal of national community, which disparaged care and cooperation in politics.

arms-reduction.rationale: Inferred from Juenger's total mobilisation and glorification of war and military values.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Inferred from Schmitt's friend-enemy politics and the preference for strong executive power over public accountability.

capital-controls.rationale: Inferred from Spengler's and Sombart's hostility to finance capital and Prussian state primacy over the economy.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Inferred from the strong, sovereign state the Conservative Revolution wanted (Schmitt), though some Weimar-era thinkers valued paramilitary units.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Juenger's Total Mobilization and Spengler's cult of duty and struggle make military obedience and national war central, so refusal is rejected.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Inferred: Prussianism and Socialism favours duty and a hierarchical corporate order over independent union bargaining.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Inferred from the movement's national-hierarchical orientation; top-ups for low earners were not discussed in the sources.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Inferred from its rejection of liberal legalism and its wish for a state free to mobilise resources; Schmitt in particular opposed legal limits on sovereign decision.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Inferred from its nationalism and hostility to the liberal international order; developing-country interests were not its concern.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Inferred: the movement sought to capture and strengthen the existing state, not dismantle it, even while rejecting parliamentary democracy.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Total mobilization and the Prussian socialism ideal call for a single, state-directed national economy under a hierarchy, not open experimentation.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Inferred: the movement treated nature as raw material to be mastered by technology (Spengler, Juenger), not as priced capital.

sacred-nation.rationale: Its core aim, per Herf, was a mythic national rebirth and a Volk community that gives individuals meaning through duty.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Inferred from its dislike of welfare-state liberalism and stress on duty over entitlement.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Inferred from its organic, Volk-centred view of the nation, which denies regional exploitation within a unified national community.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Inferred: its rejection of Enlightenment universalism and its cult of a technically-remade Worker type weaken any belief in a fixed human nature grounding rights.

public-service-media.rationale: Inferred from its rejection of liberalism and parliamentary democracy and the Nazi-era model of state-directed propaganda.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Its thinkers rejected Enlightenment universalism and held to myth and Volkisch particularity, so a single universal truth shared by all religions is inferred to be rejected.

farm-price-support.rationale: Spengler and Freyer wanted a protected, organised national economy and a rooted peasantry against liberal markets; farm support is inferred from that, as the sources do not discuss it.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Its thinkers prized military power and technology as national strength, so unilateral disarmament is inferred to be rejected; nuclear arms are anachronistic for them.

workers-own-party.rationale: Spengler's Prussian socialism wanted duty-bound corporatist bodies and rejected Marxist class parties and parliament, so a separate workers' party is inferred to be disliked.

ban-fgm.rationale: FGM is not addressed; a hierarchical but modern state that valued the nation's health would plausibly ban a harmful bodily practice, a weak inference.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Not addressed; the movement's authoritarian, traditional gender views pull against equal rights while its modern state pulls toward uniform law, so it is split.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Not addressed; Volkisch language nationalism cuts both ways here, and the sources give nothing on it.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: These thinkers wanted a strong state directing industry in the national interest and distrusted liberal legalism, so private tort-only liability is inferred to be disfavoured.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: They wanted a centralised modern state with a single sovereign, as in Schmitt, so a role for customary chiefs is inferred to be unwelcome; chiefs are anachronistic to them.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Environmental protection is not addressed; they put the nation's strength and industrial mobilisation first, so priority for the environment over liberty is inferred as rejected, though they also rejected liberty as an ideal.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: A strong authoritarian state favouring order and severity over liberal procedure would plausibly fix punishments by law, inferred from Schmitt's and Juenger's authoritarianism.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: A Volkisch national state centred on a single national culture is inferred to demand that immigrants adopt the language, though the sources do not discuss it.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Inferred from the Nazi-aligned corporatist mainstream, which replaced free unions with state-run labour bodies.

voter-id.rationale: Inferred from the nationalist, exclusionary view of the citizen body; the issue itself was not addressed.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Inferred from the volkisch idea of a national state with one authoritative spiritual order, in line with Schmitt's political theology.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: The school rejected liberal parliamentary democracy and held that rulers draw legitimacy from nation, will and leadership rather than competitive elections.

premarital-sex.rationale: Inferred from the Conservative Revolution's emphasis on duty, hierarchy and traditional moral order.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Inferred from its support for a strong state that puts national order and mobilisation above individual liberties.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Inferred from its corporatist, hierarchical view of the economy, which sits ill with an individualised liberal cash transfer.

women-suffrage.rationale: Inferred from its hierarchical, male-centred volkisch ideal of national service and mobilisation.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Inferred from its rejection of Enlightenment feminism and its traditionalist view of sex roles.

race-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from the volkisch and racial nationalism that many of its thinkers shared or were absorbed into.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Inferred from its authoritarian, traditional approach to sex roles, which rejects state bodies promoting equality.

missingStatements.text: Modern technology and industry should be embraced as instruments of national strength and tradition rather than resisted as threats to them.
missingStatements.rationale: This is Herf's defining combination of enthusiasm for technology with cultural reaction, described as a highly technological romanticism.
missingStatements.declined: Vague as a question (embracing technology while keeping tradition); tech-solves-problems and accelerate-technology cover the technology dimension.

missingStatements.text: Political unity should rest on shared myth and will rather than on rational debate and compromise.
missingStatements.rationale: Griffin's account of consciously manipulated national myth and Spengler's 'we no longer believe in the power of reason over life' place myth and will at the centre.

missingStatements.text: The comradeship of soldiers at war is the best model for national community.
missingStatements.rationale: Juenger saw front-line comradeship as the true German socialism and wanted military values kept in peacetime.
missingStatements.declined: Specific to Juenger's front-line ideal; overlaps duties-before-rights and conscription.

notes: Most answers are inferred from a small set of secondary sources because the primary texts (The Worker, Prussianism and Socialism, Man and Technics) could not be opened in full; only high and medium answers should be treated as stated positions. Juenger refused to join the Nazi party and objected to its treatment of Jews, and Spengler kept his distance too, while Schmitt joined, so racial and Nazi-state answers describe the Nazi-aligned mainstream of the strand.
